Problem associated with the method or amount of time associated with the delivery of a fluid. Time to delivery or amount of delivered entity may be affected.
Complete failure to fill as part of an automated process. For insufficient filling use "Short Fill". For excessive filling use "Overfill". For inconsistent filling use "Volume Accuracy Problem".
Excessive filling of a device. For complete failure to fill use "inability to auto-fill". For insufficient filling use "Short Fill". For inconsistent filling use "Volume Accuracy Problem".
Insufficient filling of a device. For complete failure to fill use "inability to auto-fill". For insufficient filling use "short fill". For inconsistent filling use "Volume Accuracy Problem".

Inconsistent filling of a device. This describes a problem which is observed to vary between overfilling and under filling, and may be intermittent. Use "Overfill" or "Short Fill" if problem is consistent.
Problem associated with the process of passing a substance through a porous medium, e.g., a blood clot filter for the removal of suspended matter.
Problem associated with the filter failing to remove items or substances which should have been removed.

Problem associated with the transfer of fluid between the blood and dialysate through the dialysis membrane due to a pressure gradient (trans-membrane pressure) existing between the blood and dialysate compartments.
Problem associated with the regulation and delivery of therapeutic agents (e.g. air, gas, drugs or fluids into a device or a patient under positive pressure).
Continuous flow of fluid (e.g. liquid, gas) against the intended flow direction.
Problem associated with uncontrolled flow of infusion of air, gas or fluids.
Problem associated with the increased rate of change in temperature, pressure, or other variables as a function of distance, time, etc.
Delivery at endpoint not as intended; either too low or too high.
Problem associated with fluctuations in the flow volume delivered per time, even if end volume is correct, and delivered in the correct total time.
Problem associated with the flow not being steady characterised by intermittent stoppages to the flow.
Problem associated with partial backflow, compromising the device's flow output.
Problem associated with flow rate. Flow volume delivered over time is not reaching intended flow rate.
Problem associated with the amount of gas that is inspired and expired during one respiratory cycle.
Problem associated with the inability of the device to expand or enlarge with the intended inflation agent (e.g. saline or air).
Problem associated with an insufficient dose of therapeutic agents, e.g., drugs or fluids being delivered into a patient under positive pressure.
Problem arising from the device failing to deliver the specified liquid or gas.
Failure (=complete nonperformance) with regard to the intended function of delivery.
Failure (=complete nonperformance) with regard to the intended function of infusion.
Failure (=complete nonperformance) with regard to the intended function of irrigation.
Problem related to an obstruction or blockage within the device component (e.g. tube, opening, pipe) that results in restriction of flow (including blood clotting).
Problem related to an obstruction or blockage within the device component (e.g. tube, opening, pipe) that results in no flow.
Problem related to an obstruction or blockage within the device component (e.g. tube, opening, pipe) that results in a reduction of the flow rate.
The device is difficult to flush, possibly indicating an obstruction within device.
Problem associated with the application of a force either internal or external to device that compromises the flow of fluid or gas.
Unintended decrease in pressure, compromising the device's intended function.
Unintended increase in pressure, compromising the device's intended function.
Unintended complete loss of pressure, compromising the device's intended function.
Problem associated with pump performance deviating from specifications in a way to compromise flow or infusion or dispensing.
Unintended decrease in pump speed and hence, probably, flow rate, compromising the intended function of the device.
Unintended increase in pump speed and hence, probably, flow rate, compromising the intended function of the device.
Problem associated with the device which fails to start pumping.
Unexpected/unintended cessation of pump.

Problem associated with suction equipment, which may be a manual, electrical, vacuum or pressure source operated to evacuate and remove undesired substances (air, gas, fluid, or particulates) via tubing and collection bag.
Problem associated with the removal of fluid or gas from a body cavity or device due to decreased suction.
Problem associated with the removal of fluid or gas from a body cavity or device due to increased suction.
Problem associated with the complete inability to provide suction.
Problem associated with the preparation of the device to begin pumping.
Problem associated with the device failing to begin the priming process (i.e. the process of preparation of device for the delivery of fluids).
Problem associated with not adequately preparing the device.
Problem associated with air or gas in the device (e.g. air in line).

Problem associated with any deviations from the intended performance of the device that relate to the sequence of events for activation, positioning or separation of device. Note: Deployment is synonymous with activation.
Problem associated with the activation of the device. Note: Activation includes expansion.
Problem associated with the device failing to be activated including partial activation.
Problem associated with delayed or difficult activation of the device.
Problem associated with early and unexpected activation of the device.
Problem associated with the unexpected or unintended activation of the device or a device function.  For Unintended Power Up use A070804
Problem associated with a device not responding to key or button inputs.
Problem associated with a device deactivating during use.
Problem associated with the movement of the device to an intended location.
Problem associated with the inability of the device to be positioned in a specified location.
Problem associated with the device being positioned in a location other than intended or specified.
Problem associated with users experiencing difficulty or delay to position the device to a specified location.
Problem associated with failure to move the device to an intended location.
Problem associated with difficulty moving the device to an intended location (e.g. difficulty in advancing guide wire).
Problem associated with problems introducing or inserting the device, even if the user is operating the device in accordance with the instructions for use or labeling.
Problem associated with the user experiencing difficulty when taking out the device, even if the user is operating device in accordance with the instructions for use or labeling.
Problem associated with the device caught within patient vasculature, tissue, or other device.
Problem associated with the detachment or separation of the device.
Problem associated with the device or one of its components failing to detach or separate as intended.
Problem associated with users experiencing difficulty or delay with detachment or separation of the device.
Problem associated with an early and unexpected detachment or separation of the device from the system.

Problem associated with any deviations from the documented specifications of the device that relate to the implemented and inherited design features specific to devices used for reducing risks to patient or caregiver or maintaining risks within specified levels.
Problem associated with the alarm system of the device.
The device does not display an alarm message when required.
The device fails to emit an audible alarm.
The audible device alarm cannot be heard clearly.
The device alarm system operates with delay.
Problem associated with the device providing incorrect alarm warning or alert to user.
The device alarm does not operate as expected and/or in agreement with device's specifications.
Problem associated with the feature that prevents the unsafe use of the device.
Problem associated with the device fail-safe mechanism, which did not function or function in a non effective way, compromising safe use of the device.
The device does not have a fail-safe mechanism, although such mechanism would be required for its appropriate and/or safe functioning.
Problem associated with the device failing to perform an internal self-diagnostic process to ensure normal operation during or prior to use.
Problem associated with the inability of device to turn itself off when the device is not in an operable condition.
Problem associated with setting a variable, register, or other storage location back to a prescribed state.
Problem associated with the device failing to set a variable, register, or other storage location back to a prescribed state.
Problem associated with the device failing to set a variable, register, or other storage location back to zero.
Problem associated with the device setting a variable, register, or other storage location to an inappropriate or unexpected state.
Problems with the activation of a protective measure indicator earlier than expected.
Problems with the early or unexpected activation of the elective replacement indicator.
Problem with the early or unexpected activation of the end-of-life indicator.
Problem associated with the device inability to act as a barrier for absorption of radiation energy in X-rays, gamma rays, etc.
Problem associated with compatibility between device or substances (medication, body fluid, etc.)
Problem associated with the incompatibility of any device while being operated in the same use environment thereby leading to a dysfunction between the devices.
An accessory required for the intended purpose of the device appears incompatible with device, thus compromising the intended function of the device.
A component required for the proper functioning of the device is not compatible with other components or subassemblies of the device, thus compromising the intended function of the device.
Problem associated with the incompatibility of two or more devices while being operated in the same use environment thereby leading to a dysfunction of more than one device.

Problem associated with the incompatibility of the measurement systems between and/or within device systems that are inherent to the individual device thereby leading to miscalculated or mismatched measurements from those devices, e.g., international metric system versus U.S. measurement system.
Problem associated with the ability of two or more devices which are intended to be incompatible but are able to work or fit together.

Problem associated with the presence of any unexpected foreign substance found in the device, on its surface or in the package materials, which may affect performance or intended use of the device, or problem that compromise effective decontamination of the device.
Problem associated with the undesired introduction of impurities either chemical or microbiological in nature, or of foreign matter into or onto the device.
Problem associated with the undesired introduction of a biofilm coating into or onto the device.

terms.t: Contamination of Device Ingredient or Reagent
terms.d: Problem associated with the undesired introduction of impurities either chemical or microbiological in nature, or of foreign matter into or onto the device ingredient or reagent.
Problem associated with the undesired presence of body fluid in/on the device, which are not part of the documented device specifications and requirements.

terms.t: Device Contamination with Chemical or Other Material
terms.d: Problem associated with contamination of the device with chemical substance or other non biologic material.
Problem associated with undesired microbial contamination of the device.

terms.t: Device Contaminated During Manufacture or Shipping
terms.d: Problem associated with the presence of any unexpected foreign substance found on the surface or in the package materials, which may affect optimal performance for its intended use, and which occurred during manufacture or shipping.

Problem associated with a failure during any step of reprocessing process (cleaning, disinfection, packaging, labeling, sterilization) of a used or opened from its original packaging, but unused, device.
Problem associated with the failure of the device or operator to remove any visible soil, foreign material or organism deposits on the external surfaces, crevices, and joints of the device.
Failure to properly disinfect the device when reprocessing it.
Flushing process was not executed properly.

terms.t: Problem with Removal of Enzymatic Cleaner
terms.d: Enzymatic cleaner was not removed properly.
Device was not sterilized properly during reprocessing.
Problem associated with the decontamination process not adequately removing unwanted visible soil, foreign material, or organism deposits.

terms.t: Device Contaminated at the User Facility
terms.d: Problem associated with the presence of any unexpected foreign substance found on the surface or in the package materials, which may affect optimal performance for its intended use, and which occurred at the user facility.
Problem associated with the surrounding conditions in which the device is being used such as temperature, noise, lighting, ventilation, or other external factors such as power supply.
Problem associated with any undesired acoustic energy or vibration that tends to interfere with the operation of the device.
Problem associated with compromised device performance at the ambient temperature or the storage at an inappropriate ambient temperature.
Problem associated with the visibility, odor, or toxicity of an ambient vapor or gas.
Problem associated with the visibility of molds, mildews, yeasts, and/or mushrooms in the immediate environment in which the device is being used.
Problem associated with an unsatisfactory humidity level in the storage or use environment which affects the device performance.
Problem associated with damage inflicted upon the device from water vapor or water in the immediate environment in which the device is being used.
Problem associated with the circulation of fresh air in the immediate atmosphere in which the device is being used.
Problem associated with the visibility of water vapor in the immediate atmosphere in which the device is being used.

terms.t: Device Unsafe to Use in Environment
terms.d: Problem associated with environmental condition that results in the unsafe use of the device. (e.g. electromagnetic fields, noise, vibration, microbiological contamination etc.)
Problem associated with fine solids or liquid particles such as dust, smoke, fume, and/or mist suspended in the immediate atmosphere in which the device is being used.
Problem associated with the facility-supplied medical gases such as medical air, oxygen, nitrous oxide, and nitrogen.
Problem associated with the quality of the facility-supplied power.
Problem associated with the failure of the facility's emergency power backup system(s) including generators and/or interruptible power systems (UPS).
Problem associated with the failure of primary power supplied by the facility.

Problem associated with a momentary overpower/over voltage from the utility and electrical systems of user facilities; - Problem associated with inadequate power conditioning such as the presence of fluctuation, surges, spikes, dropouts, noise and other such undesirable transients.
Problem associated with unsatisfactory installation, configuration, and/or setup of a specific device.
Problem associated with the use of the device characterized by incorrect assembly of device components, parts or constituents.

terms.t: Labeling, Instructions for Use or Training Problem
terms.d: Problem associated with device markings/labeling, instructions for use, training and maintenance documentation or guidelines.

Problem associated with the written, printed or graphic material accompanying or affixed to the device or any of its packaging. This includes verbal instructions relating to identification, technical description, and usage provided by the device manufacturers. Problems can include but are not limited to this material being unclear, missing, worn out, incorrect or inaccurate.
Any problem involving the accuracy, legibility, presence, or interpretation of an expiration date on a medical device, its labeling, or associated documentation.

terms.t: Illegible or Difficult to Read Information
terms.d: Problem associated with information unable to be read or deciphered.
Problem associated with imprecise, incorrect inexact information.
Problem associated with ambiguous, confused information.
Absence of information e.g. labeling, instruction for use.
Problem associated with an incorrect label being affixed to the device or packaging.

Problem associated with medical device label that  looks similar to another product leading to confusion. The other product may be another device or a different product such as a medicine or cleaning agent, or other product altogether.  Use A020505 for packaging look-alike issues.

terms.t: Lack of Maintenance Documentation or Guidelines
terms.d: Problem associated with user facility not receiving adequate service documentation, guidelines, or recommendations to perform preventative and corrective maintenance and performance assurance checks.

Problem associated with inaccuracies in any written, printed, or graphic matter that is affixed to the device or its packaging with any matter that accompanies the device including verbal instructions related to identification, technical description and use of device provided by the device manufacturers that is intended for healthcare professionals.

Problem associated with users being unclear and not able to follow any written, printed, or graphic matter that is affixed to device or its packaging with any matter that accompanies the device including verbal instructions related to identification, technical description and use of the device provided by the device manufactures that vary from the standard of medical care in a given environment.
Problem associated with facility not providing satisfactory initial and/or periodic user training covering operation of the device.
Problem associated with the user experiencing difficulty operating or otherwise interacting with the device, even if the operation is being performed according to labeled instructions for use.

terms.t: Device Difficult to Setup or Prepare
terms.d:
Problem associated with the user experiencing difficulty in preparing the device for use, even if the operation is being performed according to labeled instructions for use.
This includes difficulty attaching or connecting parts together.

terms.t: Device Difficult to Program or Calibrate
terms.d: The device is difficult to program, calibrate or set to desired state, even by appropriately trained user/operator.

Problem associated with the user's ability to service the device according to the manufacturer specifications relating to the device routine maintenance, i.e., periodic inspection, failure detection, repair, and care of the device to sustain or restore acceptable operating conditions.
Problem associated with the means by which the operator and the equipment communicate or interact.

The device provides a message which is unhelpful or uninformative, such as an error code without further information about the meaning or appropriate action to take.
If the message does not make sense then use A2206 - Device Provides Unintelligible Message.

The device provides an unintelligible or incomprehensible message such as an apparently random string of characters.
If the message makes sense but is not helpful then use A2205 - Device Provides Uninformative Message.
Problem associated with failure to process, service, or operate the device according to the manufacturer's recommendations or recognized best practices.
Handling of the device not in accordance with specification, prior to use on the patient.
Problem associated with the use of the device in terms of inappropriate or incorrect control settings or incorrect treatment parameters for the device's specified operation and/or intended use.

terms.t: Improper or Incorrect Procedure or Method
terms.d: Problem associated with the use of the device in terms of nonconforming to that device's intended use, specifications, procedure and process or service instructions and information provided by the device manufacturers.
Problem associated with the device which has been used for an unapproved indication or for an unapproved intended use.
Problem associated with incorrect assembly of the device or constituents after being put into use.
Problem associated with incorrect assembly of the device or constituents by the users.
Problem associated with incorrect assembly of the device or constituents during maintenance or repair.
An adverse event (e.g. patient harm) appears to have occurred, but there does not appear to have been a problem with the device or the way it was used.

A report has been received but the description provided does not appear to relate to an adverse event. This code allows a report to be recorded for administration purposes, even if it doesn't meet the requirements for adverse event reporting.

terms.t: Prophylactic Removal Due to Corrective Action
terms.d: Prophylactic removal of a device due to corrective action without malfunction or problem of the specific device involved
An adverse event appears to have occurred but there is not yet enough information available to classify the device problem.

terms.t: Appropriate Device Problem Term/Code not Available
terms.d: The device problem is not adequately described by any other term. Note: this code must not be used unless there is no other feasible code. The preferred term should be documented when submitting an adverse event report. This information will be used to determine if a new term should be added to the code table.
A feeling of falling down which can occur whether the person is standing, sitting or lying down.
Damage to the brain.
Hernia of brain substance and meninges through a congenital or traumatic opening of the skull.
A swelling in the brain caused by the presence of excessive fluid.
Unexpected increase in cerebral blood flow after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or carotid artery stenting (CAS).
Abnormal enlargement of the cerebral ventricles.
The loss of cerebrospinal fluid into the surrounding tissues or outside the body.
Changes in perception, thinking, or remembering.
A mental state characterized by a lack of clear and orderly thought and behavior.
Loss of intellectual abilities interfering with an individual's social and occupational functions.
Traumatic brain injury as a result of the action of a mechanical force on the head.
Sudden, involuntary skeletal muscular contractions of cerebral or brain stem origin.
A convulsion marked by alternating contracting and relaxing of the muscles.
A convulsion marked by prolonged contraction of the muscles.
Epilepsy caused or apparently caused by device. Do not use when epilepsy is a pre-existing condition.
A life-threatening condition characterised by a single prolonged seizure or a series of seizures without intervening full recovery of consciousness.
Decreased sensitivity affecting one or more senses
Increased sensitivity affecting one or more senses
A sensation of lightheadedness, unsteadiness, turning, spinning or rocking.
Impairment of verbal communication skills, often resulting from brain damage.
Inability to speak.
An acute inflammatory process affecting the brain parenchyma.
A functional and/or structural disorder of the brain that is acquired or congenital and characterised by mental and neurological symptoms.
Pain in various parts of the head, not confined to the area of distribution of any nerve.
A disorder characterized by an abnormal increase of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.
Bleeding within the cranium.
A level of awareness that can be described as consistently not responsive to stimuli.
A state of profound unconsciousness associated with markedly depressed cerebral activity.
Extremely weak; threatened with syncope.
A spontaneous, transient, loss of consciousness caused by insufficient blood supply to the brain.
Systematic and extensive loss or impairment of memory caused by organic or psychological factors. This may be temporary or permanent, and may involve old or recent memories.
A disorder characterized by acute inflammation of the meninges of the brain and/or spinal cord.
Neurological conditions resulting in abnormal voluntary or involuntary movement, which may impact the speed, fluency, quality and ease of movement.
Difficulty moving; distortion or impairment of voluntary movement, as in tic, spasm, or myoclonus.
Partial or complete loss of function of one or more muscles. It is usually caused by damage to the nervous system.
Paralysis of the legs and lower part of the body.
A slight or incomplete paralysis.
Paralysis of all four limbs.
The shaking movement of the whole body or just a certain part of it, often caused by problems of the neurons responsible for muscle action.
The occurrence of a single contraction or a series of contractions of a muscle.
A condition that is characterized by an irresistible urgency to move the legs to obtain relief from a strange and uncomfortable sensation in the legs.
A partial or complete loss of function of one or more of the facial muscles resulting in paralysis of the facial regions. Includes both central and peripheral facial paralysis or palsy.
Movement disorder characterized by involuntary muscle contractions.
Inability to perform particular purposive actions
Injury to nervous tissue.
Injury to optical nerve.
Injury to the central or peripheral nervous system.
Traumatic damage of the spinal cord.
Intense painful sensation along a nerve or group of nerves.
A disorder affecting the cranial nerves or the peripheral nervous system. It manifests with pain, tingling, numbness, and muscle weakness.
The loss of the sensation of feeling in an area of the body.
Injury to the peripheral nervous system.
Pain or discomfort caused by exposure of the dentin layer of tooth to thermal, tactile, or other stimuli.
A change from the patient's baseline sleeping pattern, in the hours slept and/or an alteration/dysfunction in the stages of sleep.
A term referring to disorders characterized by the disruption of normal speech. It includes stuttering, lisps, dysarthria and voice disorders.
A chronic adhesive arachnoiditis in the spinal arachnoid, with root and spinal cord symptoms similar to those caused by pressure from a tumor.
A sudden loss of neurological function secondary to hemorrhage or ischemia in the brain parenchyma due to a vascular event.
An acute neurological deficit caused by bleeding within the brain or between the brain and the skull.
An ischemic condition of the brain, producing a persistent focal neurological deficit in the area of distribution of the cerebral arteries.
conditions characterized by an alteration in the ability to or perception of touch.
Increased sensitivity to tactile stimulation.
Impairment of tactile sensitivity manifesting as partial loss of sensitivity to sensory stimuli.
Abnormal touch sensations, such as burning or prickling, that occur without an outside stimulus.
Conditions characterized by an alteration in taste function or perception
Inability to taste.
Distortion of taste.
An involuntary, compulsive, repetitive stereotyped movement.
A brief attack (from a few minutes to an hour) of cerebral dysfunction of vascular origin, with no persistent neurological deficit.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the nervous system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific injury but the relevant term does not exist.
Pressure within the craniospinal compartment is increased.
The presence of air or gas within the cranial cavity.
A condition that mimics the presence of a tumor (Pseudotumour Cerebri) or hydrocephalus, caused by chronic  increase in intracranial pressure.
A level of awareness and arousal other than normal.
A neurological state characterised by increased ability to perceive and respond.
A neurological state characterised by decreased ability to perceive and respond.
Injury to the dura mater, with or without damage to any other layer of the meninges.
Conditions characterized by an alteration in the function or perception of smell, including diminished, distorted, or lost olfactory sensation.
Diminished or absent reflex responses
Excessive clenching of the jaw and grinding of the teeth.
Change from the affected person's usual emotional state.
Apprehension or uneasiness which may be accompanied by restlessness, tension, tachycardia, and dyspnea.
A condition marked by ongoing feelings of sadness, despair, loss of energy, diminished interest/pleasure and difficulty dealing with normal daily life.
A state of physiological or psychological stress that cannot be compensated for by normal adaptive measures.
A feeling of general discomfort or uneasiness, an out-of-sorts feeling.
A feeling of agitation. Tending to become frustrated or upset easily.
A false sensory perception in the absence of an external stimulus.
Characterized by a lack of vitality or energy.
Thoughts of taking one's own life.

terms.t: Unspecified Mental, Emotional or Behavioral Problem
terms.d: The report describes a non-specific Mental, Emotional or Behavioral problem. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
A usually reversible condition characterized by the acute and sudden development of confusion, illusions, movement changes, inattentiveness, agitation and hallucinations.
A mental disorder characterized by personality change, impaired functioning and loss of touch with reality.
The sensation of struggling to remain awake.

Excessive mistrust or suspicion of people -thinking incorrectly, for example, that someone is trying to hurt you, that people are doing things to deliberately annoy you or that there is a conspiracy against you.
A reduction in the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, and/or the volume of packed red blood cells.
Anemia resulting from the premature destruction of the peripheral blood red cells.
A condition in which there is a deviation from or interruption of the normal coagulation properties of the blood.
A pathological process where the blood starts to coagulate throughout the whole body. This depletes the body of its platelets and coagulation factors, and there is an increased risk of hemorrhage.
Low blood platelet count.
Disruption of the integrity of the erythrocyte membrane causing release of hemoglobin.
An abnormally high circulating blood volume.
An abnormally low circulating blood volume.

The presence of pathogenic microorganisms in the blood stream causing a rapidly progressing systemic reaction that may lead to shock. Symptoms include fever, chills, tachycardia, and increased respiratory rate. It is a medical emergency that requires urgent medical attention.
A tumor-like collection of serum in the tissues.
The presence of an enlarged lymph node.
The white blood cell count is below the normal range, including neutropenia.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the blood or lymphatic system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
The white blood cell count is above the normal range.
Adverse events associated with the transfusion of whole blood or one of its components, most commonly a hemolytic reaction to cross-typed blood.
One or more of the blood protein levels being higher or lower than normal (e.g. Albumin, C-reactive Protein).
A disorder resulting from loss of function or tissue destruction of an organ or multiple organs, arising from humoral or cellular immune responses of the individual to his own tissue constituents.
A local or general reaction of an organism following contact with a specific allergen to which it has been previously exposed and to which it has become sensitized.
Progression of anaphylaxis into systemic shock, which is characterized by significant reduction in tissue perfusion which leads to hypoxia and hypotension, and can lead to death if untreated.
Acute immune response that occurs from exposure to an allergen. For conditions which have progressed to systemic shock, use E040201 - Anaphylactic Shock.
A regionally-limited response to an antigen, which may include inflammation, induration, erythema, pruritus or pain.
A deficiency of immune response or a disorder characterized by deficient immune response.

Indicates that antibodies directed against nuclear antigens have been detected. Almost invariably found in systemic lupus erythematosus and are frequently found in rheumatoid arthritis, scleroderma, Sjogren's Syndrome and mixed connective tissue disease.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the immune system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
Bulging or ballooning in an area of an artery secondary to arterial wall weakening.
An aneurysm that has burst, resulting in hemorrhage into adjacent tissues.
Expansion of aneurysm.

A vascular disorder characterized by thickening and hardening of the walls of the arteries. Build-up of fatty material and calcium deposition in the arterial wall resulting in partial or complete occlusion of the arterial lumen.
The blockage of a blood vessel lumen by air or solid material such as blood clot or other tissues (e.g., adipose tissue, cancer cells) that have migrated from another anatomic site.
The presence of bubbles of air in the vascular system; occurrence is related to the entry of air into the venous circulation following trauma or surgery.
Type of embolism when lumen of vessel or ductus is occluded by part of device.
The obstruction of the pulmonary artery or one of its branches by an embolus, sometimes associated with infarction of the lung.
Occlusion of the lumen of a vessel by a thrombus that has migrated from a distal site via the blood stream.
The blockage of a blood vessel by fat particles in the circulation.
The leakage of body fluid or cells from the vascular system to the surrounding tissues. This process occurs either by force or as a result of a pathologic reaction (e.g., inflammation).
A localized collection of blood, usually clotted, in an organ, space, or tissue, due to a break in the wall of a blood vessel.
The loss of blood from the circulation, including blood loss from a device connected to a patient.

A flat discoloration of the skin or a mucous membrane, larger in area than a petechia, caused by the extravasation of blood. Discolouration under the skin caused by a bleed underneath. Typically a bruise.
Extensive loss of blood due to internal or external hemorrhage.
The measurement of the mean left atrial pressure, as measured by a catheter introduced into the distal pulmonary artery, is high.
The measurement of the mean left atrial pressure, as measured by a catheter introduced into the distal pulmonary artery, is low.
Lack of oxygen in tissues, commonly due to impaired blood supply to an area of the body, resulting in impairment of tissue oxygenation.
The formation of new blood vessels.
Damage to a blood vessel resulting from a full thickness disruption in the integrity of the vessel wall.
Damage to the venae cavae, pulmonary artery, pulmonary veins or aorta resulting from a full thickness disruption in the integrity of the vessel wall.
Inflammation of any one of the blood vessels, including the arteries, veins, and rest of the vasculature system in the body.

The creation of hematoma outside the arterial wall following bleeding due to puncture of the arterial wall. Pseudoaneurysms can also occur in the heart chambers following myocardial infarction with rupture of the wall of the ventricle.
The formation of a blood clot in the lumen of a vessel or heart chamber.
Spontaneous or induced tear within the wall of a blood vessel.
Spontaneous or induced tear within the wall of the aorta
Vasoconstriction involves narrowing of a blood vessel lumen due to smooth muscle contraction in the vessel wall and leads to decreased blood flow.
Widening of a blood vessel lumen due to smooth muscle relaxation in the vessel wall and leads to increased blood flow.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the vascular system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
Inadequate blood flow to a particular area of the body.
Tissue damage caused when blood supply returns to tissue after a period of ischemia or lack of oxygen. The restoration of circulation results in inflammation and oxidative damage.
Partial or total occlusion or obstruction of the coronary ostia or artery.
Contraction of muscular walls of blood vessels
Persistent blood flow in the false lumen of a dissection following an endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) procedure.

A condition characterized by abnormally low systemic vascular resistance, often presenting with hypotension and preserved or elevated cardiac output; may be referred to as vasodilatory shock or vascular tone loss
A deviation from normal central venous pressure values
Telangiectasia, also known as Spider veins or thread veins, are prominent clusters of small, damaged blood vessels visible in the skin. They appear as thin red, blue, or purple lines.
Any variation from the normal rate or rhythm (which may include the origin of the impulse and/or its subsequent propagation) in the heart.
An electrocardiographic finding showing a state of cardiac standstill with no cardiac output and no ventricular depolarization.
Irregular heart rhythm, usually associated with a rapid rate, that is caused by abnormal electrical activity within the atrial.
A rapid heart rate, associated with a regular rhythm, that is caused by abnormal electrical activity within the atria.
An abnormally slow heart rate. Thresholds for different age, gender, and patient populations exist.
A cardiac beat originating from an abnormal site. These changes lead to extra or dropped heartbeats.
An interference with the normal conduction of electrical impulses that control activity of the heart muscle.
An electrocardiographic finding of three or more consecutive complexes of ventricular origin. The QRS complexes are wide and have an abnormal morphology. (CDISC)
A pulse that beats at irregular intervals.
Abnormally high heart rate. Thresholds for different age, gender, and patient populations exist.
Arrhythmia characterized by chaotic contractions of the ventricular muscle.
The sudden cessation of productive cardiac activity in an individual who becomes unresponsive, without normal breathing and no signs of circulation.
Increase from the normal levels of cardiac enzymes.
The presence of an acquired hole in the heart.

Acute compression of the heart caused by increased intrapericardial pressure due to the accumulation of blood or fluid in the pericardium from rupture of the heart or great vessels, penetrating trauma, or progressive effusion.
A disease of the heart muscle.
Circulatory dysfunction/insufficiency due to a decrease in the force of the cardiac contractions and / or the tone of the vascular walls. Includes diastolic and systolic dysfunction.
A tear located on a leaflet of a heart valve that prevents its complete closing, which can result in valvular dysfunction.
Weak or absent palpable pulse due to decreased arterial pulse pressure.
Inflammation of the endocardium.
Inability of the heart to pump blood adequately to fill tissue metabolic requirements or the ability to do so only at an elevated filling pressure.

A disorder of cardiac function caused by insufficient blood flow to the muscle tissue of the heart. The decreased blood flow may be due to narrowing of the coronary arteries, to obstruction by a thrombus, or less commonly, to diffuse narrowing of arterioles and other small vessels within the heart. Severe interruption of the blood supply to the myocardial tissue may result in necrosis of cardiac muscle (myocardial infarction).
Chest pain resulting from inadequate oxygen delivery for the needs of the myocardium.
A condition which occurs when blood flow decreases or stops to a part of the heart, causing damage to the heart muscle.
A below normal volume of blood pumped from the right or left ventricle of the heart per unit time.
A rupture in the mitral valve tissue due to traumatic or pathologic processes.
A bruise to the heart.
Thickening of the myocardium often due to chronic pressure overload.
Inflammation of the muscle tissue of the heart.
An electrocardiographic finding of a change in cardiac electrical activity.
Fluid collection within the pericardial sac, usually due to inflammation.
Inflammation of the pericardium.
Dysfunction of one of the cardiac valves, with incomplete valve closure or damage to a valve leaflet resulting in valvular backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the aortic valve, resulting in aortic valve backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the mitral valve, resulting in mitral valve backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the pulmonary valve, resulting in pulmonary valve backflow.
Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the tricuspid valve, resulting in tricuspid valve backflow.
Obstruction of flow across a heart valve due to immobility of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a aortic heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a mitral heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a pulmonary heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
Obstruction of flow across a tricuspid heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the heart. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
An intraoperative event that results in damage to, or abnormal function of, a heart valve. E.g. a tear in the leaflet or the chordae tendinae.
Irregular blood flow in the heart after surgical correction of a septal defect.
Increased pressure across the heart valve
An intraoperative event that results in damage to, or abnormal function of, the heart. For valvular injury, use E0624 - Intraoperative Cardiac Valve Injury
A collection of air or gas in the pericardial cavity.
The feeling of having a fast-beating, fluttering or pounding heart.
Unusual physical findings on precordial examination, including palpable vibrations, thrills, or ventricular heaves.

Progressive and life-threatening pulmonary distress in the absence of an underlying pulmonary condition, usually following major trauma or surgery. Cases of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome are not included in this definition.
Blockage of air flow in the respiratory tract.
Transient cessation of respiration.
The entry of foreign material past the trachea, and into the lower respiratory tract.
Inflammation of the lungs due to the inhalation of solid or liquid material.
A chronic respiratory disease manifested as difficulty breathing due to the narrowing of bronchial passageways.
Bleeding from the bronchial wall and/or lung parenchyma.
An acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the bronchi.
Sudden contraction of the smooth muscles of the bronchial wall.
Interference with respiration by obstruction of the larynx or trachea.

A chronic and progressive lung disorder characterized by the loss of elasticity of the bronchial tree and the air sacs, destruction of the air sacs wall, thickening of the bronchial wall, and mucous accumulation in the bronchial tree. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the air flow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough, and chest tightness. The two main types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are chronic obstructive bronchitis and emphysema.
A condition characterized by increase beyond normal in the size of air spaces distal to the terminal bronchioles, either from dilatation of the alveoli or from destruction of their walls.
A sudden, often repetitive, spasmodic contraction of the thoracic cavity, resulting in violent release of air from the lungs, and usually accompanied by a distinctive sound.
Decrease in the maximum flow rate generated during a forceful exhalation, starting from full lung inflation.
An increase of the greatest rate of flow that can be achieved during forced expiration beginning with the lungs fully inflated.
Abnormal decrease of rate of breathing.
Abnormal increase of rate of breathing.
An uncomfortable sensation of difficulty breathing. It may present as an acute or chronic sign of an underlying respiratory or heart disorder.
Nose bleed.
A decrease in the fraction of the forced vital capacity that is exhaled in a specific number of seconds.
An increase in the fraction of the forced vital capacity that is exhaled in a specific number of seconds.
Coughing up blood from the respiratory tract.
A collection of blood in the pleural cavity.
An involuntary contraction of the diaphragm against closed vocal cords, producing the hic sound.
Abnormally prolonged, rapid, and deep breathing.
A state in which there is a reduced amount of air entering the pulmonary alveoli.
A deficiency in the amount of oxygen reaching the tissues.
Displacement of structures in the thoracic cavity in one direction due to increased pleural pressure on the contralateral side.
Blockage of the nasal passages.
Abnormal permanent enlargement of the lung air spaces distal to terminal bronchiole not resulted from wall destruction, e.g. due to loss of opposite lung.
Inflammation of the throat most often caused by viral and bacterial infections.
Increased amounts of fluid within the pleural cavity. Symptoms include shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain.
An accumulation of pus in the pleural space
An acute and/or chronic inflammation focally or diffusely affecting the lung parenchyma.
Acute inflammation of the walls of the terminal bronchioles.
Abnormal presence of air in the pleural cavity.
Impaired or abnormal functioning of the pulmonary system causing multiple pulmonary issues.
Accumulation of fluid in the lung tissues causing disturbance of the gas exchange that may lead to respiratory failure.
Increased pressure within the pulmonary circulation due to lung or heart disorder.
Localized necrosis of lung tissue caused by obstruction of the arterial blood supply, most often due to pulmonary embolism.
A condition in which the blood pH is less than normal, secondary to impaired gas exchange.
A condition in which the blood pH is greater than normal, secondary to impaired gas exchange.
Cessation of breathing function.
The significant impairment of gas exchange within the lungs resulting in hypoxia, hypercarbia, or both, to the extent that organ tissue perfusion is severely compromised.
Impairment of gas exchange within the lungs secondary to a disease process, neoplasm, or trauma, possibly resulting in hypoxia, hypercarbia, or both.
An infectious disease affecting the respiratory tract.
A rupture in the sinus tissue due to traumatic or pathologic processes.
A symptom consisting of the involuntary expulsion of air from the nose.
Any kind of inflammatory process of the tonsils, pharynx, or/and larynx characterized by pain in swallowing.
Condition where there are a greater number of inhalations relative to the number of exhalations.
Interference with respiration by compression of the larynx, laryngopharynx or trachea, as well as of the carotid arteria or jugular veins.
A condition that requires mechanical life support due to inability to breath effectively to maintain normal levels of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the body.

A symptom and finding during physical examination, characterized by high-pitched, whistling sound during breathing. It results from narrowing or obstruction of the respiratory airways.  Also known as stridor.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the respiratory system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
Irritation and swelling of the upper airways
A particular type of noisy sound made by air passage across relaxed tissues during sleep.
The blockage of the nasal passage due to mucosal edema. It is usually the result of a viral infection or an allergic reaction.
Clinical spectrum with frequent episodes of either complete or partial obstruction of the upper airway during sleep. Includes sleep apnea. Also known as Sleep disordered breathing (SDB).
Pattern of symptoms as a result of nasal inflammation and/or dysfunction of the nasal mucosa. There are various subtypes, such as allergic, infectious and non-allergic (e.g. atrophic) rhinitis.
Mechanical injuries to the upper and/or lower airways. For chemical injuries or exposure use E170401 - Caustic/Chemical Burns or E2003 - Chemical Exposure
Incomplete expansion of a lung or a portion of a lung; or portion of the lung collapses or becomes airless, often due to a blockage in the airway.
Lack of moisture in the nasal mucosa
Burn to upper respiratory tract from inhalation of heated gases.
A tear in the capsular bag housing the lens.

Partial or complete opacity of the crystalline lens of one or both eyes that decreases visual acuity and eventually results in blindness. Some cataracts appear in infancy or in childhood, but most develop in older individuals. (Sternberg Diagnostic Surgical Pathology, 3rd ed.)
Edema of the mucous membrane of the eyeball and eyelid lining.
Inflammation of the conjunctiva of the eye.
Clouding of the middle area of the cornea, usually as a result of scarring due to infection, injury, or inflammation.
Inability to maintain corneal integrity; or corneal edema resulting from failure of the corneal endothelium to maintain detumescence.
Hazy, swollen cornea.
Fluid from the aqueous humor enters the corneal stroma and causes swelling.
Corneal edema of inflammatory origin associated with contact lens wear and morphologically characterized by presence of epithelial microcysts.

Very small, round vesicles containing fluid and cellular debris observed on the surface of the cornea under slit lamp examination in some types of corneal dystrophy and in wearers of extended wear lenses.
Discrete, small lesions present in the cornea as a result of corneal inflammation and, in some cases, after soft contact lens wear especially extended-wear lenses.
Superficial vascularization of the cornea with infiltration of granulation tissue.
A rupture in the corneal tissue due to traumatic or pathologic processes.
Replacement of corneal tissue with scar tissue as a result of injury to the deeper layers of the cornea.
Complications of intraocular lens surgery; usually refers to intraocular lens contact with cornea, can be intermittent or chronic.
Area of epithelial tissue loss from corneal surface; associated with inflammatory cells in the cornea and anterior chamber.

A syndrome characterized by dryness of the cornea and conjunctiva. It is usually caused by a deficiency in tear production. Symptoms include a feeling of burning eyes and a possible foreign body presence in the eye.
Inflammation of the intraocular fluids or tissues usually with microbial organisms.
Profuse lacrimation.
An infection of any part of the eye, including the eyelid.
Infection within the eye.
Damage to the eye.
Injury to the epithelium of the cornea.
Burn injury, including chemical burn, to any part of the eye.
Separation of the inner retina layers from the underlying pigment epithelium.
Damage to the retina due to toxicity, exposure to bright lights, or trauma.
A usually small tearing of the retina occurring when the vitreous separates from the retina. It may lead to retinal detachment.
Detachment of the vitreous humor from the retina.
Painful sensation in the eye.
Feeling of grittiness or having something in the eye; frequently caused by a foreign body.
Increased pressure in the eyeball due to obstruction of the outflow of aqueous humor.
Hazy ring around bright lights seen by some patients with refractive error or optical defects, e.g. cataracts, or corneal swelling.
Hemorrhage within the anterior chamber of the eye.
An accumulation of pus in the anterior chamber of the eye.
Decrease of pressure of the intraocular fluid in the eye.
Increase of pressure of the intraocular fluid in the eye, also known as ocular hypertension.
Inflammation of the iris.
Inflammation of the cornea.
Keratitis due to infection, including infection by acanthamoeba.
Accumulation of intraretinal fluid and protein in the macula, which may result in swelling and decreased central vision.

Ocular pain which may be very intense, accompanied by corneal epithelium damage, conjunctival injection, lacrimation, blepharospasm, photophobia and hazy vision following corneal edema caused by overwear of contact lenses, principally the PMMA type.
An obstruction of the pupil.
Lay term applied to any condition with dilation of conjunctival or ciliary blood vessels; innumerable causes.
Degeneration of the retina.
An acute postoperative inflammatory reaction in which a noninfectious substance enters the anterior segment and induces toxic damage to the intraocular tissues.
Clinical triad of uveitis, glaucoma, and hyphema (UGH), especially associated with the insertion of an anterior chamber intraocular lens (IOL).
Inflammation of the uvea.
An interference to normal eyesight without necessarily affecting visual acuity.
The perception of sudden or brief bursts of light.
An objective visual sensation that appears with the eyes closed and in the absence of visual light.
Spots or stringy shapes in vision, often caused by deposits, aggregates, or cell fragments in the vitreous humor or lens.
Increased sensitivity of the eyes to light causing discomfort or pain.
Decreased ability to see to a degree that requires corrective measures
The loss of visual acuity (sharpness of vision).
Severely reduced visual acuity that cannot be corrected, or total loss of vision.
Perception of multiple images from one object.
Blood extravasation in the vitreous humor.
loss or prolapse of vitreous gel.
Inflammatory intraocular reaction with clouding and cells in vitreous; often accompanies inflammation of ciliary body, iris, choroid, or retina.
Rupture of the fibrous strands connecting the ciliary body with the crystalline lens of the eye (usually at the time of cataract surgery).
The report describes a non-specific problem with the eye(s) or vision. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
A generic term used to describe abnormal sensations that bother the eyes like dryness, itchiness, burning, grittiness and excessive blinking.
Progressive deformation of the corneal structure, characterized by thinning of the cornea.
Condition where iris pigment is released into the anterior chamber and deposited in the trabecular meshwork, due to a procedure or device implantation.
Decrease in corneal endothelial cell density.
Remnant lens epithelial cell proliferation and migration to the posterior capsule.
Blood extravasation in the conjunctiva.
Blood extravasation in the retina.
Blood extravasation in the choroid.
Blood extravasation in the Optic Nerve Sheath.
Dilated pupils
Remnant lens epithelial cell proliferation of the anterior capsule.
Condition which affects the structures or function of the pupil of the eye.
A change in the shape of the corneal surface presenting as abnormal radial symmetry.
A detachment of the choroid from the underlying sclera often due to the accumulation of fluid (blood for hemorrhagic, other fluids for serous detachment) in the suprachoroidal space
Fluid accumulation in the suprachoroidal space, can lead to detachment
A feeling of general eye weakness/fatigue. (e.g. asthenopia).
Retinal vein occlusion
Any pathological condition of the macula of the eye.
Neurophysiological and psychological symptoms caused by sudden and unexpected loud noise.
Injury to the hearing mechanisms within the inner ear, caused by excessively loud noise.
Partial or complete loss of the ability to detect or understand sounds resulting from damage to the outer, middle, or inner ear structures.
A condition in which a person partially loses the ability to hear sounds in one or both ears.
A condition in which a person completely loses the hearing in one or both ears.
A noise in the ears, such as ringing, buzzing, roaring or clicking in the absence of auditory stimulation.

A feeling of movement, a sensation as if the external world were revolving around the person or as if they were revolving in space (subjective vertigo). Vertigo is medically distinct from dizziness, lightheadedness, and unsteadiness.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the ear or labyrinth. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
Earache or ear pain.
Infection of the ear.
An infectious process involving the outer ear and ear canal.
An infectious process involving the middle ear, includes acute otitis media, chronic otitis media, chronic suppurative otitis media, otitis media with effusion (OME), etc.
Inflammation (swelling and redness) to the middle ear.
An inflammation of the labyrinth in the inner ear that causes dizziness and reduced or distorted hearing.
An abnormal growth of skin cells in the middle ear, with or without infection.  May be invasive and can erode neighboring structures including bone.
Injury to the outer, middle or inner ear.
A buildup and/or blockage of earwax in the ear canal.
The condition of the abdomen being enlarged or swollen from internal pressure.
Painful sensation in the abdominal region.
Failure of the smooth muscle fibers of the gastrointestinal tract to relax at any one point of junction of one part with another.
Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity. The fluid may be serous, hemorrhagic, or the result of tumor metastasis to the peritoneum.
A thermal injury to the bowels.
A rupture in the wall of the small or large intestine due to traumatic or pathologic processes.
Irregular and infrequent or difficult evacuation of the bowels.
Passage of loose or watery stools, often occurring with increased frequency.
A symptom referring to difficult and or painful swallowing.
To belch, the casting of upwind from the stomach.
Gas or air in the gastrointestinal tract.
Inflammation of the stomach.
Thermal, chemical or radiation injury to stomach or esophagus.
Bleeding originating from any part of the gastrointestinal tract.

Flow in the opposite direction from normal, as the casting up of undigested food or gas from the stomach, or the backward flowing of blood into the heart, or between the chambers of the heart when a valve is incompetent.
Vomiting blood.
Bleeding within the abdominal cavity.
A torn, ragged, mangled wound, or an accidental cut of esophagus.
Abnormally dark tarry feces containing blood, usually from gastrointestinal bleeding.
Upper abdominal discomfort associated with an urge to vomit.
Inflammation of the pancreas.
The presence of a hole or other type of opening in the esophageal wall through which the contents of the esophagus can pass into the mediastinum.
A cut or tear of the peritoneum.
Inflammation of the peritoneum due to infection by bacteria or fungi.
Abdominal discomfort with retrosternal pain usually associated with gastroesophageal reflux, pyrosis or dyspepsia.
Bleeding originating in the retroperitoneal area.
A non-neoplastic or neoplastic (benign or malignant) disorder involving a salivary gland.
The condition of not having enough saliva to keep the mouth moist.
Excessive saliva production.
Narrowing or tightening of the esophagus
The formation of sores or a break in the wall of the stomach.
Inflammation of the oral mucosa.
Inflammation of the tongue.
Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the gastrointestinal system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
A continual or recurrent inclination to evacuate the bowels.
Free air within the peritoneal cavity.
Inflammation of the large intestine
Reduced or absent intestinal motility resulting in impaired transit of intestinal contents; may be referred to as paralytic ileus, non-obstructive ileus, or functional bowel obstruction
Inflammation of the small intestine, including duodenitis, jejunitis, or ileitis; may be associated with mucosal edema or intestinal wall thickening
Spasmodic and periodic contractions of the respiratory muscles (diaphragm and muscles of the chest and abdominal wall) without expulsion of the stomach contents
Abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) is a condition that occurs when bleeding or swelling leads to rises of pressure in the abdominal cavity that causes end-organ damage, dysfunction or failure.
Cirrhosis of the liver caused either by destruction of the intrahepatic bile ducts (primary biliary cholangitis) or blockage of the extrahepatic bile ducts (secondary biliary cholangitis).
Inflammation of the liver; usually from a viral infection, but sometimes from toxic agents.
Abnormally high level of bilirubin in the blood. Excess bilirubin is associated with jaundice.
Non traumatic damage to the liver parenchyma resulting in hepatic insufficiency.
Sustained, and severe damage to the liver with significant loss of function.
A cut or tear in the liver.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the liver or biliary system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
Sudden unexpected leakage of bile from the liver or soft tissue.
Inflammation of the bile duct.
A condition resulting from the excessive loss of fluid from the body.
Higher or lower than normal values for the serum electrolytes; usually affecting Na, K, Cl, Ca, CO2, BUN.
Higher than normal levels of sodium in the circulating blood.
Lower than normal levels of sodium in the circulating blood.
Higher than normal levels of calcium in the circulating blood.
Lower than normal levels of calcium in the circulating blood.
Higher than normal levels of potassium in the circulating blood.
Lower than normal levels of potassium in the circulating blood.
Higher than normal levels of bicarbonate in the blood.
Lower than normal levels of bicarbonate in the blood.
Higher than normal levels of phosphate in the circulating blood.
Interruption or disruption of the intake of food/nutrition.
A temporary and/or sudden feeling of intense body warmth, flushing, sometimes accompanied by sweating.
Abnormally high level of glucose in the blood.
Elevated ketones, including metabolic acidosis produced by accumulation of ketone bodies resulting from uncontrolled diabetes mellitus.
Abnormally low level of glucose in the blood.
Extreme thirst, often accompanied by chronic excessive intake of water
Repetitive loss and regain of body weight.
An imbalance of one or more hormones in the body
Menopause occurring spontaneously before 40 years of age
Low levels of one or more vitamins in the body.
Abnormally low levels of thyroid hormone
An increase in the hydrogen ion concentration in the systemic circulation that results in an abnormally low serum bicarbonate level.
Abnormally high levels of thyroid hormone
A disorder characterized by abnormally high alkalinity (low hydrogen-ion concentration) of the blood and other body tissues.
A state of nutritional deficiency or imbalance
Thyroiditis reflects inflammation of the thyroid gland.
Difficult or painful urination.
Blood in the urine.
Abnormal build up of fluid in the abdomen.
A sudden compelling urge to urinate.
An acute or chronic condition where the kidneys are not functioning normally.
An acute or chronic condition that is characterized by the inability of the kidneys to adequately filter the blood resulting in uremia and electrolyte imbalances.
Abnormally high concentration of non-protein nitrogen in the blood.
Narrowing of any part of the urethra. With or without affecting the flow of urine.
Urination at short intervals or at higher volumes; it may result from increased urine formation, decreased bladder capacity, or lower urinary tract irritation.
Accumulation of urine within the bladder because of the inability to urinate.
An inflammatory process affecting any part of the urinary tract, most commonly the bladder or the urethra.
An inflammatory process affecting the kidney.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the kidneys or urinary system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
A condition arising from the formation of renal calculi (e.g. kidney stones, bladder stones, urinary tract stones).
A chronic bladder condition resulting in recurring discomfort or pain in the bladder or surrounding pelvic region. Also known as Bladder Pain Syndrome (BPS).
Thickening of the bladder walls, including Bladder Trabeculation.
A condition of excess urine accumulation in kidney(s) that causes swelling of kidneys.
Impaired or abnormal functioning of the bladder, including sphincters.
Traumatic damage to the kidney(s).
Secretions from the vagina with a smell, color, or texture which is different from normal.
Having pain, tenderness or discomfort in the breast.

Abnormality in the breast parenchyma, identified either by palpation or imaging. These abnormalities include calcifications, breast tissue distortion, presence of areas of density, and presence of benign or malignant tumors.
Changes such as abnormal, pathological, benign, malignant, etc.
Painful or difficult coitus.
A rupture in the fallopian tube due to traumatic or pathologic processes.
Abnormal bleeding from the genitalia.
Uterine bleeding that occurs during a time not associated with the normal menstrual period.
Heavy or large blood loss during menses.
Deviations from the normal process; e.g. delayed, difficult, profuse, scanty, unusual bleeding, etc.
Excessive sensitivity or changes in sensitivity in the nipple(s)
Ulcer that develops in the nipple.
Any pelvic infection involving the upper female genital tract beyond the cervix.
Abnormal connection between rectum and vagina.
Difficulty, lack of desire, or pain associated with coitus.
Persistent or recurrent inability to achieve or to maintain an erection during sexual activity.
A rare acute life-threatening systemic bacterial noncontagious illness caused by staphylococcal exotoxins.
A rupture in the uterus due to traumatic or pathologic processes.
Abnormal connection between vagina and bladder.

terms.d: The report describes a non-specific problem with the breasts or reproductive system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
Issues related to the ability to breastfeed.
An uncomfortable feeling of itching and burning in the vaginal opening resulting from inadequate vaginal lubrication.
Pain in the pelvic area
Symmastia is a condition where the breasts join together in the middle of the chest, resulting in a lack of cleavage.
The unintentional or intentional loss of a pregnancy before 22 weeks gestation.
Expulsion of all the products of conception following medical or surgical pregnancy termination.
The uterus is not entirely emptied of products of conception following medical or surgical pregnancy termination.
Abortion brought on intentionally.
Retention in uterus of an abortus.
Spontaneous expulsion of a human fetus before it is viable.
Inflammation of the amnion.
A subperiosteal hemorrhage limited to the surface of one cranial bone, a usually benign condition seen in the newborn as a result of bone trauma.
An infection involving chorion, amnion and amniotic fluid; generally, there is also involve placental villi and from decidua.
Any abnormality either hereditary or due an influence that happen during the pregnancy until the moment of birth.
Pregnancy condition that happens when there is a developing fetus or embryo outside the uterus.

Signs or symptoms which may be indicative of distress to a fetus, which may include repetitive variable decelerations, fetal tachycardia or bradycardia, late decelerations, or low biophysical profile.
Caused by conditions such as inadequate placental function (often abruptio placentae), preeclamptic toxicity, prolapse of the umbilical cord, or complications from anesthetic administration.
Cervix that is abnormally prone to dilate without contractions in the second trimester of pregnancy, resulting in premature expulsion of the fetus.
Any Apgar score less than seven. This may be the initial or a subsequent apgar score.
Anatomic abnormality manifested during the neonatal period of physical or mechanical origin.
An abnormality that affects hearing within the first month after birth.
Complete loss of the ability to detect or understand sounds present in an infant within its first month after birth.
Partial loss of the ability to detect or understand sounds present in an infant within its first month after birth.
Injury to the brain of a newborn infant occurring around the time of birth.
The woman became pregnant despite using a contraceptive device.
Delivery of a viable infant before the normal end of gestation.
A condition of the newborn marked by dyspnea with cyanosis.
Appearance of anomalies and/or developmental defects due to exposure to an agent that can disturb the development of an embryo or fetus.
Children affected by toxins may be due to silicone breast implants and their effects on unborn children and from breastfeeding.
Injury to vaginal mucosa.

Inability to conceive for at least one year after trying and having unprotected sex. Causes of female infertility include endometriosis, fallopian tubes obstruction, and polycystic ovary syndrome. Causes of male infertility include abnormal sperm production or function, blockage of the epididymis, blockage of the ejaculatory ducts and hypospadias.
Pain in a joint.
An inflammatory process affecting a joint.

A chronic systemic disease, primarily of the joints, marked by inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures, widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, and by atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures.
A traumatic or pathological injury to the bone in which the continuity of the bone is broken.
Traumatic or pathological injury to the hip in which the continuity of either the femoral head, femoral neck, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric regions is broken.
A traumatic break in one or more of the bones in a limb.
Two or more simultaneous traumatic breaks in one or more bones.
A traumatic or pathologic injury to the bones of the skull in which the continuity of the bones of the skull is broken.
Traumatic or pathological injury to the spine in which the continuity of a vertebral bone is broken.
A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the connective tissue.
A sustained, sudden and involuntary contraction of a muscle or group of muscles.
An involuntary muscular contraction involving a muscle of the abdomen or of a hollow organ within the abdomen.
An injury to any of the fibrous bands of tissue that comprise an articulation (joint).
Problem with mastication due to pain, discomfort or loss of mobility in the jaw.
Inflammation of fascia.
Inflammation and fibrous degeneration of a muscle.
A traumatic injury to the head.
Forceful extension of a joint beyond its normal limits.
Insufficient structural and functional connection between living bone and the surface of a synthetic implant.
Failure of the fixation of a prosthetic component in the absence of infection.
Failure of the fixation of a prosthetic component in the presence of infection.
Degenerative, pathological or traumatic changes in the cartilaginous tissue of the spine leading to unwanted compression or protrusion of the disc.
An abnormal separation where two or more bones meet.
Partial dislocation of the bones in a joint.
Looseness or instability of a joint.
A finding that the flexibility of a joint is below the expected range of normal for that individual.
Immobility of the joint due to the formation of bone, cartilaginous or fibrous tissues around the joints.
Permanent restriction of a joint, usually resulting from prolonged spasticity in a muscle area.
An involuntary, persistent state of firm, tense muscles with marked resistance to passive movement.
Fibrotic joint disorder characterized by excessive collagen production and adhesions that result in restricted joint motion and pain.

Joint is blocked or becomes stuck.

Faulty healing of bone, resulting in improper anatomical alignment.
Also known as Metallosis. Includes trunnionosis, aseptic fibrosis or local necrosis secondary to metal corrosion and release of wear debris.
Abnormally low level of muscle tone.
Any injury to muscle or tendon tissue including strains.
A reduction in the strength and/or mass of one or more muscles.
Pain sensation originating from a muscle or group of muscles.
Pain in the neck area.
Limited mobility of the neck, usually accompanied by pain.
Broken bone that doesn't heal or is delayed in healing.
The formation of bone or of a bony substance outside the normal skeleton. Includes ectopic or heterotopic ossification, myositis ossificans.
Dissolution of bone; applied especially to the removal or loss of the calcium of bone.
Infection of bone or bone marrow.
Decreased calcification or density of bone tissue.
An idiopathic inflammatory disorder affecting the muscles. It presents with symmetrical proximal muscle weakness and elevated skeletal muscle enzymes.
Damage to the bones of the spine.
Inflammation of a synovial membrane.
Breakage of any portion of the tooth.
Discrepancy between the lengths of the lower or upper extremities.
The report describes a non-specific problem with the musculoskeletal system. Note: Please use E2402 if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.
One or more teeth lost/dislodged from the mouth.
Inflammation of the fluid-filled pad (bursa).
Damage of cartilage.
Impingement relating to joints. Can be e.g. implant-on-bone, implant-on-soft tissue, or implant-on-implant impingement.
An infection of the bony air cells in the mastoid bone.
Pain in the arms and/or legs.
Abnormal curvature and/or alignment of the spine.

Overuse tendon injuries characterized by a combination of pain, diffuse or localized swelling, and impaired performance. Problems include tendonitis/tendinitis and tendinosis, as well as tendon tears and inflammation of membranes around a tendon

Condition in which a closed muscle compartment's pressure increases to such an extent that the circulation is diminished, e.g. due to decrease in a compartment volume or an increase in the contents of a compartment, or both.
Bleeding into the joints
An indentation made at the edge of the bone without bone breakage.

A malignant neoplasm that develops or arises in breast tissue.

A malignant tumor of smooth muscle cells that can arise almost anywhere in the body but is most common in the uterus, abdomen, or pelvis.

A sac-like closed membranous structure that may be empty or contain fluid or amorphous material.

A disease acquired predominantly through sexual contact.

A group of rare degenerative brain disorders associated with prions for example Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).

Any disease caused by a virus.

Contact with a chemical substance through touch, inhalation, or ingestion.
Traumatic compression of the body or a part of the body.

A sudden movement downward, usually resulting in injury.

An occurrence involving any object including device and/or fragments of device being left unintentionally in the body. This includes devices left in the body as part of risk mitigation or surgical bailout procedures since their presence or location is not as originally intended.

terms.t: Device Embedded In Tissue or Plaque

A cut or tear in any tissue.
A penetrating stab wound from a needle (or other sharp object) that may result in exposure to blood or other body fluids.
Patient becomes entangled or trapped in a device.
Infection of a wound. This does not include post surgical wound infection.
Forcible tearing or disruption of tissue.

Damage to tissue due as a result of external pressure.

Traumatic damage and/or injury to the perineum.

Exposed to or contacted with blood or body fluids of another person.
Pain that is associated with an external artificial replacement device.
Failure of a surgically-induced connection between tubular structures in the body. Includes Anastomotic Leakage

Continuing discomfort due to a lack or failure of a medical approach to treat pain.

Pain occurring during a surgical operation.
A level of sedation that is greater than the intended level.
A hole or opening made through a membrane or other tissue or material.

Infection of a surgical skin incision.

Infection local to an implanted or invasive medical device.
The accidental removal of a previously inserted line from a blood vessel.

Loss of anatomical alignment after fracture reduction.

Pathological process consisting of hardening/thickening of tissue or structures.

Pain at the infusion or injection site.

Condition that relates to the presence of viable bacteria in the bloodstream, whether associated with active disease or not.

Radiolucencies observed on x-ray.

An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience that is associated with actual or potential tissue damage or described in such terms.
Pain in the chest.
Unhealthy, pale or white appearance of the face.
Lack or absence of balanced proportions between parts or organs of the body.
A condition in which an organ or body tissue drops or bulges out of place.
The drooping or downward displacement of a body part.

terms.t: Reaction to Medicinal Component of Device
terms.d: Any local or systemic adverse reaction to the medicinal component of a combination product.

accumulation of fluid in tissues perfused by the peripheral vascular system.

Complete impairment of two or more organs or organ systems. Also known as multiple organ failure.

Unusual breath odor (e.g., halitosis, fruity/sweet breath)

The substance-specific organic brain syndrome that follows the discontinuation of, or reduction in, administration or intake of an addictive substance.

terms.d: No patient involvement or, no observable clinical symptoms or a change in symptoms is identified in the patient.

Death in utero; failure of the product of conception to show evidence of respiration, heart beat, or definite movement of a voluntary muscle after expulsion from the uterus, with no possibility of resuscitation.

Patient diagnosis was clinically significant delayed as a consequence of device performance.

Situation in which the use of the device impedes or affects a subsequent medical procedure or use of a medicine or device. The time elapsed between the use of the device and the medical procedure is not a factor. It is not necessary for the device to have broken or malfunctioned.
Use of the device has lead to worsening of the existing disease or condition, as a direct consequence of device use

Patient requires admission to or extension of stay in an intensive care unit.
Patient required emergency transfer to a different facility because of the need for an additional level of care.

Exposure to, or intake of, an excessive amount of a substance.

A non-serious injury, illness or impairment which can be treated with minimal or no intervention, including monitoring only.
A severe injury, illness or impairment which requires hospitalization or medical intervention.
Disease that persists over a long period of time, cannot be prevented by vaccines or cured by medication, nor do they just disappear.
Any physical or mental impairment that interferes with an individual's ability to perform desired activities.
Patient suffered an illness or injury which if not treated would be fatal.

An incorrect diagnosis or classification of an illness or other problem.

Patient experiencing a complication that is well documented in association with the device or procedure.
Decrease in lifetime/ lifespan of an individual. Decline in the normal duration or in average life.
Patient required sedation or additional sedation.

Surgery that is more complicated, more comprehensive or more extensive than planned (e.g. percutaneous to open surgery).

Any event type, which results in imminent risk of death, serious injury, or serious illness to more than one individual, that requires prompt remedial action.

Requirement for imaging that was not originally planned.
Patient required additional or unexpected IVD testing.
Patient required an unforeseen medical intervention, excluding surgery, which was not on the original treatment plan.
Use of an additional or alternative device require to achieve optimal outcome.
